views.name: department_degree_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT d.department_id, d.department_name, COUNT(dp.degree_program_id) AS degree_count FROM Departments d LEFT JOIN Degree_Programs dp ON d.department_id = dp.department_id GROUP BY d.department_id, d.department_name
views.description: Per-department counts of degree programs (one row per department with department id, name, and the number of degrees offered)
validated_on: How many different departments offer degrees?

provenance.question: Which department offers the most number of degrees? List department name and id.
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Find the department (name and id) that offers the highest number of degrees.
Required outputs: department name; department id
Filters: Consider all departments present in the database; Count degrees offered by each department across all degree records; If multiple departments tie for the highest count, include all tied departments
Sort/limit: order by degree count descending; limit to the maximum count (no fixed numeric limit)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows at the declared grain (department_id, department_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT department_id, department_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM department_degree_counts GROUP BY department_id, department_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: degree_count matches count of Degree_Programs per department (recomputed from base tables)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM department_degree_counts ddc LEFT JOIN (SELECT department_id AS dep_id, COUNT(degree_program_id) AS expected_count FROM Degree_Programs GROUP BY department_id) dp ON ddc.department_id = dp.dep_id WHERE COALESCE(dp.expected_count,0) <> COALESCE(ddc.degree_count,0)

tests.purpose: Keys are not NULL: department_id and department_name must be present for every row
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM department_degree_counts WHERE department_id IS NULL OR department_name IS NULL

positive_subgoals:
Task: Count the number of distinct departments that offer degrees
Required outputs: a single integer value representing the count of different departments that offer degrees
Filters: Consider only rows where a department is indicated as offering a degree (i.e., include each department that offers at least one degree)

views.name: courses_with_section_counts
views.body_sql: SELECT c.course_id, c.course_name, COUNT(s.section_id) AS section_count FROM Courses c LEFT JOIN Sections s ON c.course_id = s.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id, c.course_name
views.description: For each course, the course id and name together with the count of associated sections (0 if none); useful as a cohort or per-course measure for other queries.

provenance.question: What are the names and ids of every course with less than 2 sections?
provenance.rewrite:
Task: Return every course's name and id for courses that have fewer than 2 sections.
Required outputs: course name; course id
Filters: include only courses whose count of associated sections is less than 2 (i.e., 0 or 1 section)

tests.purpose: No duplicate rows per grain (course_id, course_name)
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT course_id, course_name, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM courses_with_section_counts GROUP BY course_id, course_name HAVING cnt > 1)

tests.purpose: Every course in base table appears exactly once in the view
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Courses c LEFT JOIN (SELECT course_id AS v_course_id FROM courses_with_section_counts) v ON c.course_id = v.v_course_id WHERE v.v_course_id IS NULL

tests.purpose: section_count matches COUNT of Sections per course (including zero) recomputed from base tables
tests.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses_with_section_counts v LEFT JOIN (SELECT course_id, COUNT(section_id) AS real_count FROM Sections GROUP BY course_id) s ON v.course_id = s.course_id WHERE COALESCE(s.real_count, 0) != v.section_count
